headline: High risk: shared filesystem/MCP and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action hazards between Gemini CLI and Windsurf.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can use MCP and read/write local files, so attacker-controlled content in shared workspace files can flow from Gemini CLI to Windsurf or vice versa and be treated as instructions. Gemini CLI’s filesystem/git sharing and Windsurf’s clipboard/workspace surfaces make this plausible in default coding workflows, though not as directly dangerous as a raw web-to-agent bridge.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo
IF either agent ingests file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the two agents
Require manual review of any file both agents may read
Use separate git branches per agent
Turn off MCP servers unless explicitly needed
Add a provenance banner to agent-generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches shell environment, repo files, and user-provided directories, while Windsurf reads workspace files and can use clipboard. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive code or secrets to the other through files or copied content; the blast radius is multiple work products, not just one document.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory tree
IF secrets or proprietary source code are present in that tree
mitigations: Keep secrets in a separate unshared directory
Mount only a minimal project subset into each agent
Clear clipboard before switching agents
Disable automatic file ingestion where possible
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification. Gemini CLI explicitly shares state via filesystem and git, and Windsurf shares via local filesystem, so concurrent edits can clobber each other or corrupt repo state without locking. This is a default-dangerous overlap with potentially irreversible loss.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF either agent auto-applies edits while the other is active
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for isolation
Require explicit commit review before merge
Disable auto-execute/auto-apply modes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s Cascade loop can treat prior agent output as actionable context, and Gemini CLI can emit code, shell commands, or file edits that Windsurf may then extend or execute. Because both have command execution and write authority, a mistaken or malicious first-step output can cascade into destructive follow-on actions without verification.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Gemini CLI output as authoritative
IF either agent is allowed to execute commands or edits without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human approval step between agents
Require tests before any generated patch is applied
Restrict one agent to read-only review
Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI is open-source with Google-account optional login and broad API egress, while Windsurf is closed-source and runs as user in the editor process with model-proxy traffic. The pair can move source code and open files through different vendors and retention regimes, creating a compliance mismatch risk, though no specific residency or regulated-data violation is proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated or proprietary data is processed by both agents
IF organizational policy requires a single approved processor or retention regime
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings
Use separate accounts for each tool
Disable cloud features where possible
Document data flows before deployment
